evidence.paraphrase: Mudgala tells Dakṣa the campaign’s purpose. Matsara and demons approach Śukra, request consecration as their king and receive his agreement. Named chiefs assemble; Veda-knowing Brahmins consecrate Matsara with Ṛg/Yajus/Sāman formulas, Uśanas directing the rites. The assembly rejoices and returns home.

evidence.paraphrase: Matsara summons the Asuras to conquer the three worlds. Fourfold forces muster with arms, trees, rocks and mountains: infantry, decorated elephants, swift horsemen, chariots and other animal mounts. His decorated chariot has one hundred asses; both sons ride horses ahead, Virocana and other chiefs around him.

evidence.paraphrase: Demon forces defeat terrestrial rulers: some flee, some surrender, warriors die fighting. Sons of dead rulers are installed as tributaries; surrendered kings retain office. Demons govern rulerless regions and are stationed beside local kings. Matsara rejoices after conquering the islanded earth.

evidence.paraphrase: Demons destroy Nāga gardens in Pātāla. Vāsuki, Takṣaka, Kambala and Aśvatara lead resistance: arms and missiles first repel demons; returning chiefs repel Nāgas. Serpent poison-flames burn demons, weapons and mounts; Śukra’s vidyā removes poison. A Garuḍa missile produces bird assailants, burnt by Vāsuki’s poison-fire. Virocana and chiefs themselves become Garuḍas by māyā and overwhelm Nāgas.

Kubera hears the news and flees to Śiva on Kailāsa; demons occupy Alakā and march with captive Varuṇa against Yama.

He disables Yama’s buffalo and fells Yama. Rising, Yama strikes him with Kāladanda; the staff instead falls to earth, and Viṣayapriya captures him. Demons praise the son’s feat.

evidence.paraphrase: Demons proceed with captive Yama to Amarāvatī. Agni, Vāyu, Viśvedevas, Sādhyas, Rudras, Vasus, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Vidyādharas, planets, moon, sun and Ādityas join Indra on Airāvata with vajra. Seven nights end in demon flight and fainting chiefs. Sundarapriya attacks the gods; Indra’s vajra does not move him. He disables Airāvata, seizes Indra by the foot and captures him. Other gods die, fall, flee or are captured; Matsara gains heaven.

evidence.paraphrase: Fleeing gods ask Kaśyapa to protect them and release Indra. With Vasiṣṭha, gods and sages, Kaśyapa petitions Brahmā to restore proper stations. Brahmā admits Matsara’s Śiva-boon makes him unconquerable and takes them to Viṣṇu, who also admits inability. They seek Śiva, who explains his own fierce-austerity grant and inability to destroy the demon. Viṣṇu chooses refuge at Kailāsa rather than submission, predicts Matsara will take Vaikuṇṭha and Satyaloka but spare Kailāsa out of devotion. Śiva remains anxious.

evidence.paraphrase: Matsara occupies Indra’s throne, uses Airāvata, receives frightened celestial entertainers and redistributes divine offices to demon chiefs. He resents Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra not paying homage. Andhaka is sent to summon them under threat, finds Satyaloka and Vaikuṇṭha empty, then enters Kailāsa and receives a seat. He delivers the demand. Śiva asserts that Matsara wins through his boon and threatens to burn him; he releases Andhaka because he is an envoy and orders him to report.

evidence.paraphrase: Andhaka praises Kailāsa’s unmatched splendour. Chiefs urge attack; Matsara credits his own austerity and karma, rejecting Śiva’s boast as giver. He argues desire-driven action yields gains and Brahman-dedicated action liberation, and claims world creation, preservation and destruction depend on karma rather than the three gods. Demons march to Kailāsa, wound Śiva’s guards, who flee and report.

Bull-mounted Śiva advances. Confused armies counter weapons and wrestle; chiefs enter named duels while Matsara watches. He counters Viṣṇu’s thousand-arrow shower and fells him with a hundred. Śiva’s trident is ineffective and falls; Matsara nooses his neck and draws him like a bound animal. He taunts Śiva that both owe capacity to karma, captures other gods and enjoys Kailāsa.

Some sages keep rites in wild forests, while others abandon duties from fear. Sacrificial exclamations cease; gods suffer starvation and cannot devise his destruction.

evidence.paraphrase: Wandering Dattātreya arrives, a fearless naked yogin and Gaṇarāja devotee. Gods honor him, massage his feet and offer fruit. Śiva asks a destruction strategy, describing displacement and starvation. Dattātreya says Śiva’s own claim to unique lordship is Matsara in his heart; conquer envy through yoga and Gaṇeśa worship. He recounts his own one-syllable worship and non-separation from Gaṇeśa, prescribes that worship, tells Śiva first to destroy inner Matsara then the demon, and leaves.

evidence.paraphrase: Śiva repeats Dattātreya’s counsel; gods and sages worship Gaṇeśa with the one-syllable mantra for a thousand divine years. They use diverse seats, fasting or leaves/air/water, breath control, toe-standing, mental worship, flowers and circumambulation. Vakratunda appears as radiant Brahman, lion-mounted, elephant-faced, four-armed with noose/goad and boon/fearlessness gestures, Siddhi left and Buddhi right. The alarmed petitioners ask gentleness; he identifies himself and softens his radiance. They worship with sixteen services and begin a hymn.

He explains that gods, humans, Nāgas and the world belong to the five-element/three-guṇa/eight-envelope domain from which Matsara has no fear, making destruction difficult, yet promises their welfare.

They offer obedience and say one could destroy Matsara. Vakratunda explains that he created the demon through māyā for play: immediate annihilation would end the play. He orders battle in his presence and says a form without the eight envelopes can kill him instantly. Gods and sages rejoice; the whole host goes to the city named Īrṣyā.

Frightened gods petition immediate protection; lion-mounted Vakratunda with noose/goad promises rescue and roars, terrifying all worlds and demons. Chiefs offer to fight while Matsara watches.

evidence.paraphrase: Prahlāda’s Anala missile burns gods and mounts; Indra prepares Megha missile, but Prahlāda cuts his bow before release. Yama staffs Mahiṣa down; Virocana swords Yama down. Varuṇa nooses Virocana, but Andhaka cuts the noose and maces Varuṇa. Vāyu swords Andhaka down; Śambara clubs Vāyu down. Virocana’s arrows fell Kubera.

Śiva answers that Vakratunda came to reduce earth’s burden, reversed their former time through changed karma, and will enable him to destroy them. evidence.paraphrase: Vakratunda sends eight chief Gaṇas with their troops: Pramoda, Āmoda, Brahmapriya, Yogapriya, Svānandabhoktṛ, Jñānamaya, Sarvaga and Sarvavit. Their look restores gods from fainting, fatigue and wounds, with doubled energy. Kavi restores demon forces to life and health. Gaṇas’ weapons sever demons; Brahmapriya seizes Śukra and throws him in a distant cave. Demons resolve to die fighting or rescue their guru, disable gods again, but the armed Gaṇas fell the chiefs and kill or disable the army.

Matsara threatens a one-arrow victory, invokes claimed earth-splitting and mountain-crushing strength, and offers Vakratunda life under his command in the forest while threatening the instigating gods and sages.

evidence.paraphrase: Vakratunda says he is neither god, human, Asura, Nāga, Gandharva nor mountain, nor a creature from varied birth-origins or the eight envelopes, but joy-giving Brahman. He came to restore gods and sages; Matsara’s boon-merit has loosened through accumulated sin. He offers survival if Matsara surrenders and abandons hatred of dharma and gods. Astonished, Matsara respectfully asks how attribute-free Brahman can have form and favor gods over demons.

evidence.paraphrase: Vakratunda explains creation as play with each being’s own dharma, his indwelling control through Puruṣa and Prakṛti, and conditional impartiality. When gods abandon duty to uproot demons or obstruct austerity, he inspires and grants demons boons against them. When demons abandon duty to uproot gods, he reveals their vulnerable means through the gods or takes form against demons the gods cannot conquer. He remains Brahman in both when they follow duty. Matsara oppressed gods through abandoning his own dharma, so he came against him.

evidence.paraphrase: Vakratunda shows his Brahman form in a point; by the grace and fruit of that vision Matsara receives divine sight. He sees the form beyond body/embodied, guṇas and māyā, with attributed body, attribute-free elephant head and their yoga unity. He bows, hymns the deity’s Brahman/yogic form, four arms, lion mount, Siddhi and Buddhi lordship, and seeks refuge and passage beyond worldly existence. He repeatedly falls at the feet and stands with folded hands.

evidence.paraphrase: Vakratunda declines to destroy a surrendered devotee, offers a boon, and promises Matsara’s hymn sovereignty, health, wealth, family and four aims. Matsara requests firm devotion, affection for Vakratunda’s devotees, and a place/livelihood with welfare. Vakratunda grants unwavering devotion and directs him to protect beings following their dharma and devotees. He must cause no obstruction wherever the deity’s image is worshipped or remembered at beginnings. Elsewhere he may act as an Asura, take fruits from karma/knowledge actors and rule in their hearts; toward devotion he must act as servant. Matsara accepts joyfully.

Matsara returns to his station with demons, abiding peacefully; demons then return to their separate homes. He mentions Dhundhirāja becoming Śiva’s son for Divodāsa’s pacification, manifestation before Vāmana to grant a boon, and Brahmā’s obstructed creation after failing to remember Vakratunda: Matsara entered him; refuge in the deity removed the obstacle. evidence.paraphrase: Dakṣa requests origins and battles of the eight incarnations; Mudgala begins Vakratunda. At Indra’s yearly accession festival, Śiva comes with Pārvatī, Skanda and Nandīśvara; Viṣṇu with Lakṣmī and Viṣvaksena; Brahmā with Vedas and Prajāpatis. Sun/planets, Agni, Dharmarāja, Kubera, Varuṇa, Ādityas, Manus, Vasus, Rudras, Sādhyas, Vidyādharas, Viśvedevas, Aśvins, Śeṣa, Gandharvas, Apsarases, Nāgas, Yakṣas, sages, Rākṣasas, celestial women and Cāraṇas attend. Hāhā, Hūhū, Tumburu and Nārada participate in music, while Rambhā performs. All depart when Indra prematurely closes the festival.

He soon masters study, marries Madakarā, then receives the five-syllable formula from Śukra. His thousand divine years without food and Pāśupata initiation diminish the sun and fire light and disturb beings, leading gods/sages to seek Śiva, who arrives with Pārvatī and Gaṇas.

narrative_events.details: Mudgala tells Dakṣa the campaign’s purpose. Matsara and demons approach Śukra, request consecration as their king and receive his agreement. Named chiefs assemble; Veda-knowing Brahmins consecrate Matsara with Ṛg/Yajus/Sāman formulas, Uśanas directing the rites. The assembly rejoices and returns home.
narrative_events.outcome: Matsara is consecrated demon king.

narrative_events.details: Matsara summons the Asuras to conquer the three worlds. Fourfold forces muster with arms, trees, rocks and mountains: infantry, decorated elephants, swift horsemen, chariots and other animal mounts. His decorated chariot has one hundred asses; both sons ride horses ahead, Virocana and other chiefs around him.
narrative_events.outcome: Army marches to conquest.

narrative_events.details: Demon forces defeat terrestrial rulers: some flee, some surrender, warriors die fighting. Sons of dead rulers are installed as tributaries; surrendered kings retain office. Demons govern rulerless regions and are stationed beside local kings. Matsara rejoices after conquering the islanded earth.
narrative_events.outcome: Earth is subordinated under tribute and surveillance.

narrative_events.details: Demons destroy Nāga gardens in Pātāla. Vāsuki, Takṣaka, Kambala and Aśvatara lead resistance: arms and missiles first repel demons; returning chiefs repel Nāgas. Serpent poison-flames burn demons, weapons and mounts; Śukra’s vidyā removes poison. A Garuḍa missile produces bird assailants, burnt by Vāsuki’s poison-fire. Virocana and chiefs themselves become Garuḍas by māyā and overwhelm Nāgas.
narrative_events.outcome: Māyā transformations overcome the first failed bird missile.

narrative_events.details: Śeṣa comes conciliating, asks why fellow Pātāla residents wage war, and addresses demons as brothers. Virocana demands submission to Matsara’s universal authority or destruction. Śeṣa agrees, offers annual tribute and jewels, withdraws with Vāsuki and others. Victorious demons march against Varuṇa.
narrative_events.outcome: Pātāla settles through annual tribute.

narrative_events.details: Matsara sends Varuṇa an ultimatum: submit in office or be killed. Makara-mounted Varuṇa advances with noose and aquatic forces. Virocana, Mahiṣāsura, Śumbha and Andhaka fight them. After three days demons fall; Kāvya restores their awareness, battle resumes and Virocana captures Varuṇa. Kubera hears the news and flees to Śiva on Kailāsa; demons occupy Alakā and march with captive Varuṇa against Yama.
narrative_events.outcome: Varuṇa captured; Alakā occupied after Kubera’s flight.

narrative_events.details: Buffalo-mounted Yama advances with staff, Death, diseases and attendants. Five days of fighting defeat demons until Viṣayapriya fights Death and afflicts diseases. He disables Yama’s buffalo and fells Yama. Rising, Yama strikes him with Kāladanda; the staff instead falls to earth, and Viṣayapriya captures him. Demons praise the son’s feat.
narrative_events.outcome: Viṣayapriya captures Yama despite the Death-staff attack.

narrative_events.details: Demons proceed with captive Yama to Amarāvatī. Agni, Vāyu, Viśvedevas, Sādhyas, Rudras, Vasus, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Vidyādharas, planets, moon, sun and Ādityas join Indra on Airāvata with vajra. Seven nights end in demon flight and fainting chiefs. Sundarapriya attacks the gods; Indra’s vajra does not move him. He disables Airāvata, seizes Indra by the foot and captures him. Other gods die, fall, flee or are captured; Matsara gains heaven.
narrative_events.outcome: Sundarapriya captures Indra; Matsara rules heaven.

narrative_events.details: Fleeing gods ask Kaśyapa to protect them and release Indra. With Vasiṣṭha, gods and sages, Kaśyapa petitions Brahmā to restore proper stations. Brahmā admits Matsara’s Śiva-boon makes him unconquerable and takes them to Viṣṇu, who also admits inability. They seek Śiva, who explains his own fierce-austerity grant and inability to destroy the demon. Viṣṇu chooses refuge at Kailāsa rather than submission, predicts Matsara will take Vaikuṇṭha and Satyaloka but spare Kailāsa out of devotion. Śiva remains anxious.
narrative_events.outcome: Gods cluster at Kailāsa; their expectation will be challenged.

narrative_events.details: Matsara occupies Indra’s throne, uses Airāvata, receives frightened celestial entertainers and redistributes divine offices to demon chiefs. He resents Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra not paying homage. Andhaka is sent to summon them under threat, finds Satyaloka and Vaikuṇṭha empty, then enters Kailāsa and receives a seat. He delivers the demand. Śiva asserts that Matsara wins through his boon and threatens to burn him; he releases Andhaka because he is an envoy and orders him to report.
narrative_events.outcome: Andhaka returns with Śiva’s refusal.

narrative_events.details: Andhaka praises Kailāsa’s unmatched splendour. Chiefs urge attack; Matsara credits his own austerity and karma, rejecting Śiva’s boast as giver. He argues desire-driven action yields gains and Brahman-dedicated action liberation, and claims world creation, preservation and destruction depend on karma rather than the three gods. Demons march to Kailāsa, wound Śiva’s guards, who flee and report.
narrative_events.outcome: Matsara attacks his former boon-grantor’s domain.

narrative_events.details: Śiva arms with Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Kāma, Vasus, Kubera, moon, sun, Agni, Vāyu, Kālāgni Rudra, Bhairavas, Vīrabhadra, Nandin, Bhṛṅgin, Puṣpadanta, Mahākāla, Mahākālī and Kārttikeya. Bull-mounted Śiva advances. Confused armies counter weapons and wrestle; chiefs enter named duels while Matsara watches. Seven days/nights end with gods overpowering and felling the demon chiefs and sons.
narrative_events.outcome: Gods gain a temporary victory.

narrative_events.details: Matsara enters roaring and showers arrows: Senānī, Agni, Nandin, Vīrabhadra, sun, moon, Vāyu, Kālāgni Rudra, Mahākālī, Bhṛṅgin’s Gaṇas, Kubera and Brahmā fall. He counters Viṣṇu’s thousand-arrow shower and fells him with a hundred. Śiva’s trident is ineffective and falls; Matsara nooses his neck and draws him like a bound animal. He taunts Śiva that both owe capacity to karma, captures other gods and enjoys Kailāsa.
narrative_events.outcome: Śiva and divine defenders are captured.

narrative_events.details: Matsara assigns Kailāsa to Sundarapriya, Vaikuṇṭha to the son here written Vijayapriya, Satyaloka to Prahlāda, and Indra’s region to Virocana. He creates Matsarāvāsaka on earth. He releases Śiva and gods with permission to go wherever they wish provided they obey his orders. They shelter anxiously in mountain valleys and caves.
narrative_events.outcome: Divine captives are released under Matsara’s command.

narrative_events.details: Matsara orders gods’ images broken and cast into water, and installs his images in regions, settlements and houses. He coerces Brahmins to perform sacrifice, Gāyatrī and Agnihotra in his name and promises wealth and heaven; feeding demons pleases him. Some sages keep rites in wild forests, while others abandon duties from fear. Sacrificial exclamations cease; gods suffer starvation and cannot devise his destruction.
narrative_events.outcome: Suppressed worship produces divine deprivation.

narrative_events.details: Wandering Dattātreya arrives, a fearless naked yogin and Gaṇarāja devotee. Gods honor him, massage his feet and offer fruit. Śiva asks a destruction strategy, describing displacement and starvation. Dattātreya says Śiva’s own claim to unique lordship is Matsara in his heart; conquer envy through yoga and Gaṇeśa worship. He recounts his own one-syllable worship and non-separation from Gaṇeśa, prescribes that worship, tells Śiva first to destroy inner Matsara then the demon, and leaves.
narrative_events.outcome: Dattātreya prescribes inner reform and one-syllable worship.

narrative_events.details: Śiva repeats Dattātreya’s counsel; gods and sages worship Gaṇeśa with the one-syllable mantra for a thousand divine years. They use diverse seats, fasting or leaves/air/water, breath control, toe-standing, mental worship, flowers and circumambulation. Vakratunda appears as radiant Brahman, lion-mounted, elephant-faced, four-armed with noose/goad and boon/fearlessness gestures, Siddhi left and Buddhi right. The alarmed petitioners ask gentleness; he identifies himself and softens his radiance. They worship with sixteen services and begin a hymn.
narrative_events.outcome: Vakratunda manifests and accepts worship.

narrative_events.details: Gods and sages hymn Vakratunda’s forms and yoga unity, ask lasting devotion and destruction of Matsara for the afflicted world. Vakratunda promises the hymn will confer siddhis and desired objects and that he will remove Matsara. He explains that gods, humans, Nāgas and the world belong to the five-element/three-guṇa/eight-envelope domain from which Matsara has no fear, making destruction difficult, yet promises their welfare.
narrative_events.outcome: Vakratunda accepts the rescue request and states its difficulty.

narrative_events.details: Vakratunda remembers his army; Pramoda, Āmodaka and elephant-faced, four-armed Gaṇas manifest, variously lion-, mouse-, peacock-, Śeṣa- or horse-mounted. They offer obedience and say one could destroy Matsara. Vakratunda explains that he created the demon through māyā for play: immediate annihilation would end the play. He orders battle in his presence and says a form without the eight envelopes can kill him instantly. Gods and sages rejoice; the whole host goes to the city named Īrṣyā.
narrative_events.outcome: Vakratunda deliberately permits the campaign instead of immediate annihilation.

narrative_events.details: Matsara enjoys celestial company and all mentally wished objects through austerity and boon. A sky-voice announces Vakratunda’s arrival to kill him; he faints. Demons search the sky unsuccessfully and restore him. He invokes immunity against eight-envelope beings. Prahlāda and chiefs argue the defeated gods may have produced an illusion, dismiss the voice, and obtain permission to find and kill them.
narrative_events.outcome: The warning triggers a demon reconnaissance rather than surrender.

narrative_events.details: Searching chiefs see elephant-human Vakratunda praised by gods, fear the warning is true and return to report rather than risk dying before reporting. Vakratunda is encamped five yojanas from Īrṣyāpura. Matsara first pales, then orders his army to attack. Frightened gods petition immediate protection; lion-mounted Vakratunda with noose/goad promises rescue and roars, terrifying all worlds and demons. Chiefs offer to fight while Matsara watches.
narrative_events.outcome: Matsara’s fourfold host advances; chiefs begin battle.

narrative_events.details: Prahlāda-led demons rain weapons; Viṣṇu-led gods respond. Countered missiles, swords, maces, nooses and wrestling generate casualties and dust that hides friend from foe. Blood settles the dust; matching fourfold units fight one another. Wounded troops and alternating advances/falls continue without night rest for five days, with neither side prevailing.
narrative_events.outcome: Five-day stalemate opens the chief-led reversals.

narrative_events.details: Prahlāda’s Anala missile burns gods and mounts; Indra prepares Megha missile, but Prahlāda cuts his bow before release. Indra’s vajra fells Prahlāda; Mahiṣa maces Indra unconscious. Agni flames Mahiṣa, who becomes water and floods him, cuts Agni’s śakti and becomes a buffalo to fell him with horns. Yama staffs Mahiṣa down; Virocana swords Yama down. Varuṇa nooses Virocana, but Andhaka cuts the noose and maces Varuṇa. Vāyu swords Andhaka down; Śambara clubs Vāyu down. Virocana’s arrows fell Kubera.
narrative_events.outcome: Successive interventions reverse both sides’ advantages.

narrative_events.details: Viṣṇu’s mace splits Virocana’s chest leaving him dead-like; discus fells Andhaka, arrows fell Śambara, and discus/mace kill or disable demons. Prahlāda recovers, wounds gods, fights Viṣṇu with mace and fells Garuḍa with sword. As Viṣṇu’s discus approaches, Prahlāda remembers Janārdana and releases a Nārāyaṇa missile. It repels the discus, burns gods, hits Keśava’s heart and leaves him unconscious, dead-like.
narrative_events.outcome: Nārāyaṇa missile defeats the discus and disables Viṣṇu.

narrative_events.details: Seeing gods and sages burnt, Śiva uses Pināka to release Pāśupata. It fights Nārāyaṇa missile in the sky; the gods rejoice. Śiva then throws trident, kills many demons, strikes Prahlāda’s heart and fells him. Other chiefs die or faint; Matsara’s two sons Sundarapriya and Viṣayapriya approach Śiva angrily.
narrative_events.outcome: Śiva temporarily defeats the chiefs; sons enter.

narrative_events.details: Dakṣa asks for more detail; Mudgala answers that even great gods cannot recount all Vakratunda’s power. The sons challenge Śiva, promising to kill him, Vakratunda, gods and sages. Śiva answers that Vakratunda came to reduce earth’s burden, reversed their former time through changed karma, and will enable him to destroy them. Sons counter his arrows; their Pāśupata missile nullifies his trident, hits his heart and fells Śiva unconscious.
narrative_events.outcome: Even the newly confident Śiva falls to the sons’ missile.

narrative_events.details: Vakratunda sends eight chief Gaṇas with their troops: Pramoda, Āmoda, Brahmapriya, Yogapriya, Svānandabhoktṛ, Jñānamaya, Sarvaga and Sarvavit. Their look restores gods from fainting, fatigue and wounds, with doubled energy. Kavi restores demon forces to life and health. Gaṇas’ weapons sever demons; Brahmapriya seizes Śukra and throws him in a distant cave. Demons resolve to die fighting or rescue their guru, disable gods again, but the armed Gaṇas fell the chiefs and kill or disable the army.
narrative_events.outcome: Śukra’s capture removes the rescuing guru from the active battle.

narrative_events.details: Both sons challenge Pramoda’s Gaṇas and rain arrows. Sarvaga and Sarvavit counter the arrows and destroy demon troops. When the frightened sons prepare Agni missiles, two axes arrive before release and sever their heads. Survivors report both sons certainly dead, while they cannot tell if Prahlāda and others are dead or dead-like; they urge Matsara to abandon pride and surrender to protect the remaining demons.
narrative_events.outcome: Both sons die; survivors counsel surrender.

narrative_events.details: News of his sons’ death makes Matsara faint; restored after two muhūrtas, he laments lost children, supposedly failed immortality/fearlessness boon, and fate’s victory over effort. Elders comfort him: bodies die, self does not; relatives must perform funerary rites. They urge ritual duty, attack or surrender, and avoiding giving enemies joy by grief. Matsara instead takes the surviving army to battle.
narrative_events.outcome: Matsara chooses battle after consolation and alternative counsel.

narrative_events.details: Gods warn Vakratunda about Matsara’s sovereignty, timely rain, fruit, suppressed disease/theft, monopolized worship and sacrifices, displaced gods and disabled sages, seized women and immunity from eight-envelope beings. Vakratunda reassures them and advances lion-mounted with one tusk, noose and goad. Matsara threatens a one-arrow victory, invokes claimed earth-splitting and mountain-crushing strength, and offers Vakratunda life under his command in the forest while threatening the instigating gods and sages.
narrative_events.outcome: Final confrontation begins with threats and invocation of immunity.

narrative_events.details: Vakratunda says he is neither god, human, Asura, Nāga, Gandharva nor mountain, nor a creature from varied birth-origins or the eight envelopes, but joy-giving Brahman. He came to restore gods and sages; Matsara’s boon-merit has loosened through accumulated sin. He offers survival if Matsara surrenders and abandons hatred of dharma and gods. Astonished, Matsara respectfully asks how attribute-free Brahman can have form and favor gods over demons.
narrative_events.outcome: Matsara moves from threats to a doctrinal question, without a physical final duel.

narrative_events.details: Vakratunda explains creation as play with each being’s own dharma, his indwelling control through Puruṣa and Prakṛti, and conditional impartiality. When gods abandon duty to uproot demons or obstruct austerity, he inspires and grants demons boons against them. When demons abandon duty to uproot gods, he reveals their vulnerable means through the gods or takes form against demons the gods cannot conquer. He remains Brahman in both when they follow duty. Matsara oppressed gods through abandoning his own dharma, so he came against him.
narrative_events.outcome: The apparent favoritism is explained as restoring disrupted dharma.

narrative_events.details: Vakratunda shows his Brahman form in a point; by the grace and fruit of that vision Matsara receives divine sight. He sees the form beyond body/embodied, guṇas and māyā, with attributed body, attribute-free elephant head and their yoga unity. He bows, hymns the deity’s Brahman/yogic form, four arms, lion mount, Siddhi and Buddhi lordship, and seeks refuge and passage beyond worldly existence. He repeatedly falls at the feet and stands with folded hands.
narrative_events.outcome: Divine sight leads to praise and surrender.

narrative_events.details: Vakratunda declines to destroy a surrendered devotee, offers a boon, and promises Matsara’s hymn sovereignty, health, wealth, family and four aims. Matsara requests firm devotion, affection for Vakratunda’s devotees, and a place/livelihood with welfare. Vakratunda grants unwavering devotion and directs him to protect beings following their dharma and devotees. He must cause no obstruction wherever the deity’s image is worshipped or remembered at beginnings. Elsewhere he may act as an Asura, take fruits from karma/knowledge actors and rule in their hearts; toward devotion he must act as servant. Matsara accepts joyfully.
narrative_events.outcome: Matsara survives under restricted protective/obstructive duties.

narrative_events.details: Seeing Matsara at peace, gods and sages rejoice and hymn Vakratunda as Brahman encompassing and transcending forms, cosmic elements, deities, senses, creation/preservation/destruction, karma fruits, family and natural forms. They praise the demon’s transformation to peace and world’s joy, admit the deity exceeds Vedas, scriptures and yoga comprehension, and stand silent with folded hands. Vakratunda welcomes the praise.
narrative_events.outcome: Peace prompts final hymn and boon offer.

narrative_events.details: Vakratunda promises the hymn desired enjoyments, descendants, enjoyment/liberation, siddhis and insight. A thousand repetitions free a prisoner; recitation forgives offences, and twenty-one repetitions on twenty-one days grant what is contemplated. The praising gods/sages will be free of obstruction and devoted to their own dharma. Offered a boon, they request unwavering devotion as sufficient for all siddhis; he grants it.
narrative_events.outcome: Gods and sages receive unwavering devotion.

narrative_events.details: Vakratunda vanishes before gods and sages and dwells in Svānanda. Saddened gods and sages return to their own stations contemplating him. Matsara returns to his station with demons, abiding peacefully; demons then return to their separate homes. Mudgala explains Vakratunda creates, preserves and destroys and through incarnations restores gods, demons and humans to their respective duties.
narrative_events.outcome: Divine offices and ordinary homes are restored; Matsara lives peacefully.

narrative_events.details: Mudgala says Vakratunda’s incarnations are innumerable, beyond exhaustive narration by great gods, sages or Vedas. He mentions Dhundhirāja becoming Śiva’s son for Divodāsa’s pacification, manifestation before Vāmana to grant a boon, and Brahmā’s obstructed creation after failing to remember Vakratunda: Matsara entered him; refuge in the deity removed the obstacle. These are explicit brief previews, not fully extracted arcs.
narrative_events.outcome: Chapter39 closes the campaign and previews distinct stories.

narrative_events.details: Dakṣa asks how Brahmā worshipped Vakratunda. Mudgala recalls Gaṇeśa creating five divine lords and empowering them through austerity/boon. Beginning creation without remembering or worshipping Gaṇeśa, Brahmā prides himself on indispensability: without his creation, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Śakti and sun lack their functions. Many-eyed/many-faced Vighna hosts batter and toy with him. He relinquishes pride, takes refuge, remembers and hymns Gaṇeśa; the hosts vanish.
narrative_events.outcome: Humiliation and recollection remove the immediate obstruction.

narrative_events.details: Freed of obstacles, Brahmā propitiates Vakratunda with six-syllable mantra, feeding on air, standing on toe-tip, holding unwavering mental focus. After a divine thousand of austerity, disturbing beings, Vakratunda comes lion-mounted, three-eyed, elephant-faced, four-armed, with noose/goad/boon/fearlessness, Siddhi/Buddhi, Cintāmaṇi, Śeṣa at navel and red body. Brahmā fears the radiance and requests gentleness. Vakratunda softens it, explains the form ordinarily belongs to Svānanda and manifested through Brahmā’s devotion, then offers wishes.
narrative_events.outcome: Gentle manifestation prompts Brahmā’s hymn and boon request.

narrative_events.details: Brahmā praises Vakratunda’s Brahman, lion/elephant/four-arm form and Siddhi/Buddhi, requests unwavering devotion, unobstructed creative capacity, and the deity dwelling at home as son through māyā, freeing parental bondage and allowing continuous nurture/worship. Vakratunda grants all: creative power, obstacles removed by remembrance, desired objects, and rescuing sonhood through māyā/aṃśa; hymn grants all and Brahmanhood. He vanishes; Brahmā creates the whole animate/inanimate three worlds properly and rests remembering Vakratunda.
narrative_events.outcome: Creation restored; meditation-son promise awaits fulfilment.

narrative_events.details: Wind shakes Brahmā and Dambha manifests from his body-tremor as a great four-armed armed man. Asked identity, he claims birth from Brahmā’s tremor and sonhood, requests name, place and livelihood. Brahmā laughingly names him Dambha because of his boast, permits movement everywhere and enjoyments. Dambha bows and circles him, reaches earth, resents perceived disrespect and vows to remove Brahmā’s pride. He seeks Kavi, receives a mantra, and worships Brahmā foodless on one foot for ten thousand years, disturbing creation. Pleased Brahmā arrives with gods, astonished at his wooden-stillness and offers a boon.
narrative_events.outcome: Dambha’s retaliation motive leads to intense worship of his origin deity.

narrative_events.details: Offered wishes, Dambha hymns Brahmā as threefold Brahmā/Viṣṇu/Śiva and all creation. He asks three-world rule, no death from five-element beings, no equal in battle, undivided sovereignty with health. Brahmā grants all requested and any contemplated object’s success, then disappears. Dambha establishes beautiful Śobhana city on earth. Śukra summons demons, comes with Brahman-knowing sages and has Brahmins consecrate him at auspicious time. The festival ends with chiefs remaining in the city.
narrative_events.outcome: Brahmā’s grant supports Dambha’s demon kingship.

narrative_events.details: Suhuṇḍa, Huṇḍa, Rukmaketu, Madyapa, Sakopa, Krodhāsura, Kāmāsura, Rāsabhāsura and other chiefs urge conquest as Dambha’s servants. He agrees, summons Śukra and accepts his counsel, then marches with fourfold forces, defeats terrestrial kings and Pātāla Nāgas, and goes to heaven. Indra’s vajra burns and crushes demons and makes them flee; Dambha’s discus fells Indra, arrows harm gods. Recovering Indra flees to live; Dambha sits on Airāvata and Indra’s throne.
narrative_events.outcome: Dambha conquers three worlds; Indra abandons his office.

narrative_events.details: Indra and gods take refuge in Brahmā, then Viṣṇu and Śiva. Śiva angrily challenges Dambha; forty days of destructive battle follow. Dambha’s arrows fell divine chiefs. Śiva’s trident fells Dambha, who rises immediately and hurls discus, felling Śiva for half a prahara. Regaining consciousness, Śiva flees with gods to the forest. Dambha installs demons in Satyaloka, Vaikuṇṭha, Kailāsa, Amarāvatī and other divine cities, then returns to Śobhana ruling three worlds.
narrative_events.outcome: Dambha supplants divine offices after reversible defeats on both sides.

narrative_events.details: Dambha orders karma destroyed. Demons bind and beat Brahmins, break sacrificial spaces and trees, destroy tīrthas and temples. Some Brahmins die or abandon duties, others flee forests; sacrificial exclamations and social dharma cease. Gods, dependent on ritual food, appeal to Brahmā as creator/provider and giver of fearlessness: without karma and food they face starvation and death.
narrative_events.outcome: Suppression of sacrifice provokes divine appeal for rescue.

narrative_events.details: Unable to devise rescue, Brahmā advises one-syllable worship of Vakratunda. Gods/sages worship; he meditates on the previously seen Siddhi/Buddhi-bearing form. After a hundred years he sees the speaking form in his heart, then it emerges with Siddhi and Buddhi. Vakratunda says he arose from Brahmā’s meditation, is dhyānaja, and fulfils the former requested sonhood. Brahmā bows and worships all three. The narrative calls him mental son, Siddhi/Buddhi daughters, and describes Vakratunda as with wife/wives (sabhāryaka) while all prepare a hymn.
narrative_events.outcome: Promised sonhood is fulfilled by meditation-origin, not womb birth.

narrative_events.details: Brahmā with gods/sages hymns the all-form Brahman deity and marvels that the meditated Siddhi/Buddhi-bearing Brahman came out as his son. Brahmā and Brahmins perform birth rites; on day eleven name him Siddhibuddhipati. He plays as a child, Sāvitrī nurses him, and his deeds please mother and father. At two years, with Siddhi/Buddhi, he asks why father dwells sorrowfully in forest. Brahmā tells Dambha’s story. The child promises to destroy Dambha and restore offices, goes lion-mounted with Siddhi/Buddhi near the city, and sends Indra to demand own-dharma, restored sacrificial food and social order. Dambha spares Indra as envoy, otherwise threatens imprisonment, and sets battle on fifth day. Indra reports and is praised.
narrative_events.outcome: A new child manifestation offers rescue and attempts conciliation.

narrative_events.details: Dambha summons Kavi/Śukra, prostrates, receives a gold seat and asks who Siddhi/Buddhi and their lord are. Śukra explains Siddhi as alluring māyā and people’s pursuit of worldly/otherworldly/Brahman fulfilment, left at Gaṇeśa’s side; Buddhi as knowledge/mind with five citta states and innumerable variants, at his right. Both māyās were formed from the deity’s own limb for play; Svānanda is Brahman and his abode. Brahmā requested sonhood to remove parental bondage; this deity came accordingly. He warns Dambha to surrender because this form will restore dharma and destroy him.
narrative_events.outcome: Guru explains the opponent’s identity, powers and manifestation purpose.

narrative_events.details: Dambha asks why impartial Gaṇeśa, from whom dharma/adharma arise, protects one and destroys the other. Kāvya explains an ordered world with separate places: greed-driven excess adharma strengthens Asuras and weakens gods, prompting Gaṇeśa to restore dharma; excessive dharma threatens demon root-destruction, so he grants demons boons to restore adharma’s assigned place. Neither party is self/other to him; greed-driven imbalance draws intervention. Dambha meditates privately, concludes that seeking siddhi or welfare while abandoning their lord causes failure, resolves surrender and sleeps fearlessly with Gaṇeśa in his heart.
narrative_events.outcome: Doctrinal answer changes Dambha’s decision before battle.

narrative_events.details: Next morning Dambha abandons Asura disposition and tells assembled demons before Śukra that guru taught him to surrender to Vakratunda, Brahman everywhere, neither god-only nor demon-only lord. Angry demons abandon him and return home. Joyful Dambha and Kāvya go outside to Gaṇeśa, prostrate, worship and hymn his Brahman, yoga, impartial, elephant-faced/Siddhi-Buddhi-lord forms. He falls again; Gaṇeśa raises him.
narrative_events.outcome: Dambha surrenders with his guru; army declines to accompany him.

narrative_events.details: Gaṇeśa promises Dambha’s hymn joy, family/wealth/grain, relief of mental/physical affliction and troubles; regular once/twice/thrice-daily recitation pleases him. He came to kill but spares the surrendered devotee. Dambha requests firm devotion, instructions for livelihood and a stable place. Siddhibuddhipati grants unwavering devotion and own-station residence without fear for a long time; gods are not higher nor Dambha lower, all pleasing when faithful to own duty. Dambha must destroy undertakings begun without remembrance, make ritual actions fruitless without first worship, and protect beloved devotees free of Dambha disposition; acts lacking initial remembrance/worship become his karma-share.
narrative_events.outcome: Survival, devotion and conditional obstruction/protection duties replace battle.

narrative_events.details: Gaṇeśa disappears after assigning Dambha’s duties. Gods/sages acclaim victory and return radiant and fearless to their own stations; demons dwell untroubled in Pātāla cavities. Mudgala concludes Dambha’s pacification and Brahmā-sonhood and promises attentive listeners/tellers freedom from Dambha fear, Brahman, desired objects, prosperity and freedom from obstacles. He explicitly transitions to Vāmana.
narrative_events.outcome: Divine offices restored and demons peacefully resident; next arc is Vāmana.

narrative_events.details: Dakṣa asks Vāmana’s story. Mudgala introduces Kaśyapa, his senior virtuous wife Aditi, and gods including Indra born to them; opposing demons are also sage’s sons, defeated by Viṣṇu’s varied forms. They seek Kāvya, who advises100 Aśvamedhas with concealed hostility, making Bali Indra and demons celestial enjoyers. Bali, born of Virocana, is Viṣṇu-devoted and dislikes adharma. Yet he begins the first sacrifice remembering Viṣṇu and omitting Gaṇeśa. Vighna decides to consume its ritual fruits, enters Indra’s heart; Indra fears100 sacrifices will replace him and asks Viṣṇu to destroy them. Vighna then enters Viṣṇu’s heart as time-form.
narrative_events.outcome: Neglected initial worship creates obstruction through the divine opponents.

narrative_events.details: Viṣṇu tells Indra that Aditi and Kaśyapa previously worshipped him intensely for100 years and requested his sonhood; he agreed and will fulfil it now to stop Bali’s sacrifice. Forgetting Bali’s devotion, Viṣṇu is born Vāmana to Kaśyapa in Aditi, but cannot displace mighty Bali. He asks father Kaśyapa for means; receives Vakratunda’s six-syllable mantra, goes to Vidarbha and worships foodless for10 years, meditating Gaṇeśa. Vakratunda appears through mantra/austerity, lion-mounted, four-armed, one-tusked, elephant-faced, red, with Siddhi/Buddhi and noose/goad. Vāmana rises, bows and begins hymn.
narrative_events.outcome: Vāmana seeks Gaṇeśa’s aid after initial inability to move Bali.

narrative_events.details: Vāmana hymns Vakratunda as obstacle remover/giver, indwelling lord, and eminent forms including Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śambhu, Indra, sun, moon, Yama, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Kubera, Agni, Nirṛti, Śeṣa, Śukra, Sanatkumāra and Guha. He dances with tears and horripilation, losing body-awareness in exclusive devotion. Pleased deity offers wishes, promises hymn siddhi, desired objects and final Svānanda liberation. Vāmana requests firm devotion, Bali brought within his power, the deity’s appearance whenever remembered, and freedom from obstruction. Gaṇeśa agrees and disappears; Vāmana installs him, establishing Ad oṣa field in Vidarbha.
narrative_events.outcome: All requested granted, with deity installed at Adoṣa.

narrative_events.details: After worshipping Vakratunda and bowing to Kaśyapa, Vāmana reaches Bali’s sacrifice. Sages marvel at radiant short Vedic student; Bali rises, bows, worships and offers a gift. Śukra understands purpose and the initial worship omission producing a Viṣṇu-form obstacle. Vāmana asks land for three steps; Bali grants with devotion. Remembering Gaṇeśa, Vāmana becomes Virāṭ, covers heaven with one step and earth with second, demands place for third. Grieving Bali cannot answer; angry Viṣṇu binds him as debtor to a Brahmin and tells him to go to Naraka. Bali realizes his Gaṇeśa omission has brought this treatment even from his chosen Viṣṇu, and turns to Gaṇeśa for rescue.
narrative_events.outcome: Bali is bound for unfulfilled third step, then seeks Gaṇeśa.

narrative_events.details: Bali hymns Gaṇeśa as obstacle lord, all-form/impartial Brahman, Siddhi-Buddhi lord and māyā-remover; confesses own pride/envy and repeated offences, asks protection from falling into Naraka, and explains refuge gives gods freedom from illusion/obstacles. A sky-voice promises surrendered Bali no fear of Naraka through remembrance. His hymn frees readers/hearers of that fear, grants four aims and increases devotion; joyful Bali keeps meditating.
narrative_events.outcome: Bali receives explicit protection from Naraka before debt is discharged.

narrative_events.details: Vighna leaves Viṣṇu, immediately restoring understanding. Vāmana realizes he harmed his full devotee Bali and a Brahmin debt could send him to Naraka; he seeks Gaṇeśa and remembers him. Gaṇeśa appears immediately, receives worship from Viṣṇu and gods/sages. Gaining insight from the sight, Bali offers his body and asks the third foot placed on his head. Viṣṇu agrees, discharging the Brahmin debt, and begins hymn with assembly.
narrative_events.outcome: Both understand; third-step head gift discharges debt.

narrative_events.details: Vāmana hymns Gaṇeśa’s supremacy/māyā, begs forgiveness and sacrificial fruit for Bali, acknowledging Bali’s belief in Viṣṇu’s superiority led to omitted worship. Gaṇeśa says he had earlier promised Naraka through Viṣṇu’s hands, but now Bali has taken bodily/mental/verbal refuge and Viṣṇu also petitions. He orders finishing sacrifice with him first; Bali thereby gains all sacrifices’ fruit, but current fruitlessness lets him experience offence. Bali will be Indra after current Indra retires; for now establish him in Pātāla. All approve; Bali completes the final sacrifice placing Gaṇeśa first. Deity vanishes, gods return home; hearing the arc grants wishes.
narrative_events.outcome: Sacrifice repaired; Pātāla placement ordered and future Indra office promised.
